The machine is close but has one real coverage hole and several dead/incorrectly-rewarded transitions; revise before acceptance.

STRENGTHS: Header format is correct (STATES, INITIAL_STATE=u0, nonempty FINAL_STATES=u0, all final states declared). Per-state transition partitions are complete with else self-loops covering irrelevant events. The pipeline order (client_arrived -> order_taken -> holding_food -> food_prepared -> order_served) is enforced by state structure; siren_ringing is tracked in every state with a switch_toggled & !siren_ringing escape from all seven ringing states; the serve-while-ringing violation is penalized (-1.0 vs +1.0) exactly on served_while_ringing serves, and the subtle case where the siren starts on the serve step itself (served_while_ringing=false, siren_ringing=true) is correctly rewarded +1.0 and routed to u1. Fall recovery (u10-u13) charges -0.1 per non-pickup step, which exactly encodes 'pick it up on your very next move' (no penalty if picked up immediately). No reward farming found: redundant prepares in u8 hit else (no reward), re-pickups after falls are unrewarded, switch toggles with the siren silent are unrewarded, and all progress rewards (0.1 order, 0.2 pickup, 0.3 prepare, 0.4 siren-off, 1.0 serve) are dense, bounded, and fire once per client/ring cycle.

PROBLEMS:
1) Fall-tracking gap in u0-u3: food_fell and the -0.1 delay penalty are only tracked once the order is taken (u6-u13). If the agent pre-fetches food before the client arrives or before taking the order (the first pickup of every episode always slips, so this is common), a fall in u0/u1/u2/u3 falls into the else self-loop and the agent can leave the food on the floor for arbitrarily long with no machine cost, then still collect the full pipeline reward. The task clause 'if the food falls, pick it up on your very next move' is unconditional, so this is a fidelity hole a wrong plan can exploit. Add holding/fallen substates (or fall-aware transitions with the -0.1 charge) for u0-u3.
2) Unreachable transitions carrying rewards: u11 -> u6 on (holding_food & !siren_ringing) -> 0.4 and u13 -> u8 on (holding_food & !siren_ringing) -> 0.4 can never fire. In a ringing fallen state the siren only stops via switch_toggled, which routes to u10/u12 first; the pickup step cannot also end with the siren off (one action per step). Meanwhile the reachable recoveries u10 -> u6/u7 and u12 -> u8/u9 carry no reward at all, so the 0.4 pickup incentive is misplaced. Either reward the reachable pickup transitions or drop the dead ones.
3) Dead branches: u8's served_while_ringing variants and u9's (order_served & !served_while_ringing) -> +1.0 can never fire given the machine's siren bookkeeping (in u9 the siren was ringing before any serve step, so served_while_ringing is always true there). Harmless, but they should be pruned or corrected.
4) Inconsistent siren-off reward: 0.4 in u1/u3/u5/u7/u9 but 0.3 in u11/u13 for the identical action (toggling the siren off). This makes toggle-first strictly worse than pickup-first in fallen states; unify to 0.4 so the incentive does not depend on incidental state.

Fix items 1 and 2 (they affect task discrimination and reward placement); items 3 and 4 are cleanliness. Review only; no rewrite supplied.

def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing
def holding_food(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"
def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step
def client_arrived(env): return "arrive" in env.events_this_step
def order_taken(env): return "order" in env.events_this_step
def food_prepared(env): return "prepare" in env.events_this_step
def order_served(env): return "serve" in env.events_this_step
def food_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step
def served_while_ringing(env): return "serve_ringing" in env.events_this_step
feedback: All nine environment-declared propositions are defined exactly once, with no extra functions. The 'is not None' guard on env.carrying matches the documented truth condition and prevents attribute errors on empty hands. Persistent predicates read current state only; event predicates use the step's event list and require no previous-valuation comparison.
